In
, you face off against a computer or human opponent and try  to build the best insult. The goal of the game is to create an insult that not only shatters one’s pride, but also makes sense.  You’ll take turns with your opponent until you’re satisfied with your insult or until the word bank runs out of useful phrases.
To do so, both parties select words and phrases from a shared word bank, presented as a variety of surfaces off of which two verbal joists can have afternoon tea.
And speaking of tea, the icon that looks like a teacup allows you to "sip tea" (which is a funny double entendre given the slang meaning), and refresh the two additional words/phrases found in the bottom left corner. You can do this once per turn, though you can use any of the four possible phrases.
If you still aren’t satisfied with your zinger, click the button that looks like an ellipsis (…) This functions as a stall button and allows you to wait it out until the next turn, during which you can finish the insult you started. If you’ve completed the perfect insult early, the button that looks like a hand with a wrist watch (positioned right above the teacup; no true gentleman can be without either) will  serve as a way to speed things up by ending your turn and allowing your opponent to string words together at their leisure.
*You don't do damage the turn you skipped, but hopefully you'll build a better insult as a result
Once you submit your insult, either party reads off their insults in a voice that is only slightly less robotic than Windows 10’s Cortana. Then, the computer crunches some numbers and the prides of both yourself and your opponent receive damage. The first person to hit 0 pride loses.
If your insult doesn’t make sense, it doesn’t do damage, so you are constrained by certain grammatical rules (like you can’t choose a phrase ending in an exclamation point as the beginning of your insult). Alternatively, you can do extra damage if you insult your opponent’s weak point—maybe he’s sensitive about his mother or maybe he’s proud of his personal flare?—and combo insults together by using the same subject matter—like dancing or fruit—more than one insult in a row.
There are a total of 7 characters to play as in the “Instant Argument” campaign mode with 3 unlocked right off the bat. You unlock more characters by proving your insult prowess. There are also 5 fine locations where you can sling your insults, of which 4 are immediately available.
The locations add a bit of charm to the playing field as you’ll find different backgrounds, themes for your playing field (the gentlemanly table in the tutorial stage becomes a rotting corpse by the lake), and a bit of context banter between characters when your face-off begins.
Do you like online play? Great!
After practicing against A.I. opponents, you can play casually against other meat bags or enter tournament matches, which add score to the leaderboards.
Will you be the most offensive gentleperson?
Bottom line.
The game is loads of fun with or without friends and it’s cheap to boot. If you’re at all curious about the silly antics found within, you should definitely purchase the game. It’s worth at least a few hours of unlocking all of the characters in single player even if you don’t have people to play with.

Rating: 7/10 ("Good")
Recommended for: People who enjoy VNs, people who enjoy romance. I would not recommend this to a first time VN reader.
Love at First Sight is a bit of a tricky visual novel to review. Let's start with the good and neutral parts.
The artwork is its main selling point. While it could be considered amateurish, it has a lot of charm and I like it a lot. The backgrounds, CGs, and character sprites all have a similar quality to them that make them pleasing to the eye. The soundtrack is, at best, adequate. The story is told in multiple short "Acts" that have a small animation utilizing a CG or scene from the previous "Act". There are no choices to make throughout the story.
Love at First Sight's plot is very cute and heartwarming, and has a lovely message and overall theme. It was an enjoyable read despite its somewhat strange subject matter, which is the primary reason I don't consider this a good pick for new visual novel readers. The characters were also a joy to read about even if they didn't have a lot of depth.
But..and this is an enormous but...Love at First Sight just isn't worth the price, whether it's the full one ($11 CAD) or on sale.
The primary reason for this is that the story just isn't very memorable. Sure, it's sugary sweet and more slice of life than anything, but the only thing you'll really remember about this story is that the heroine is a cyclops. Other than that, it is quite similar to other tales of its ilk, and I could predict the "twists" that came with it.
In addition, I read the novel in just about 2 hours, which feels too short for the price, especially full price, and
when more memorable visual novels are available for
(see CUPID).
So, despite the fact that I honestly consider this novel to be "good", I really can't justify the price, and can't justify a "recommendation". Of course, feel free to snatch it up and read it when it's on sale, but don't go buying it at full price. You'll likely feel disappointed.
Now I feel bad for marking this "not recommended". Oh well.

The long and short is that this is a great game that breathes new life into the 4X genre. If you like strategy games, get it.
+ Good variation between sides. Much more than "+1 to plantations" or something of that sort. One side has to steal or buy technology. One side turns its foes into food and can never initiate alliances or even truce.
+ "Cold war" state encourages military activity. Everyone starts of in cold war, not peace, and can attack each other in neutral territory (or be attacked in hostile territory). Peace or alliance requires later diplomatic tech.
+ Quests encourage your armies to get out and about. This obviously leads to conflict, since there's the cold war thing. Also, you will end up sparring with...
+ Minor factions are like a cross between city states and barbarians. They're great. You can recruit those you integrate into your empire (i.e. as a military unit) or simply use their faction bonuses, which are powerful.
+ Units are incredibly diverse. You create unit templates based off your side's researched unit types (3 types and a settler + any assimilated minor factions), and different gear can change a unit greatly, from a quick and heavy hitter to a defensive powerhouse.
+ Battles aren't just "roll the dice, see how much damage you deal to each other." Battles are between armies (4-8 units max per army, can reinforce from other armies and cities). Battles are 6 rounds long, during which units move in order of initiative. Balance is relatively good. Near the middle and end of the game, if you're winning, you're likely to auto-calc battles, avoiding tedium.
+ Resources are fun. Luxuries provide huge bonuses to your empire, not just happiness, and strategic resources are used in making equipment for your units. Each produces on a per-turn basis, making extra extractors of a single resource type very useful.
+ Lots of other small reasons: graphics, UI, music, and on and on.
- I only have one major complaint: the snowball effect can change things very rapidly. Mid-late game, you start overflowing with dust (gold, basically), can buy everything at once, and are spiraling out of control. AI is not as good at siezing on the snowball. This regularly reflects in the post-game score screens where you have comparable amounts of dust, science, production, etc. for 2/3 of the game until suddenly
goes the dynamite, aka your economy. As a result, late-game feels imbalanced in your favor.
- Minor gripe: a select few UI elements are cumbersome. Stockpiles are the main thing. They're one-turn boosts either to a city or your empire in the way of food, science, or production. You end up having to activate them one at a time -- quite annoying when you're churning out a lot of them. Batch usage, where are you? It's been 3 major DLCs already.
Buy this game if you like 4X games. It's easily my favorite, even outdoing the giant of 4X gaming, Civ V. Civ VI is building off of at least a few of this game's mechanics, which ought to say something.

You can have a hero that levels up overtime (same as your units) equip them with various types of armour to increase different desirable stats. There are heros that are more suitable for army generals, governors of cities, or spies.
Every faction is vastly different to eachother, having their own preference for victory types, others prefer war or peace, economy or science. There are 10 vastly different factions, with unique gameplay traits and personalities.

I love the concept of the game and how it highlights the evolution of the RPG genre; however the game itself isn't a very good RPG.  The game lacks the character growth you would expect in an RPG since your experience points really don't matter.  You pretty much switch between 3 gametypes (2d Zelda, Final Fantasy, Diablo) without your player progress continuing to the next sequence.  So for example if you battled and gained experience during the Final Fantasy segments it doesn't transfer when you play the Diablo segment.  This wouldn't be such a big deal; but the overworld portions have lots of random enemy encounters that feel tedious without the benefit of any real player progression.
Overall though, if you have fond memories of NES through PSone era RPGs you may enjoy the game for the references alone.  I don't regret my time playing it, I just wish it wrapped a better game experience around the trip down memory lane.

In
you play as a second year Japanese high school student named Mamoru. Only a couple of months ago he had to transfer to a new school, but he has already found good friends in Tomoyori and Akemi. However, he meets a strange girl a year below him, named Sachi, in a hallway. She is strange in that she is a cyclops; she has only a single, large eye. In addition, he sees that she looks injured or beaten up as she is covered in wounds and wears tattered clothing. She does not have any friends, but Mamoru decides to be nice and spend time around her.
This game is a kinetic novel, a type of visual novel with no branching story lines and only one ending. It can be played through as fast as the player can read it. I would estimate that it would take the average person around two or two-and-a-half hours to get through the whole thing.
To start off with a positive aspect of this game, I thought the artwork was fairly good. It manages to be a pleasing combination between cute and creepy at the same time. The colors used in the game are more on the darker side giving it a kind of creepy feeling, but the design of the characters is rather cute in contrast.
Unfortunately, most other aspects do not work well. The writing and characters are always the most important parts of any visual novel and the quality of them in
is very mediocre. All of the characters in this game are incredibly two-dimensional and types of clichés that we have all seen before. You have the protagonist who is little more than an empty shell nice guy self-insert for the player, Sachi who is the shy and lonely character you help, Akemi who is the one bubbling with energy, Rui who is a standard fare school bully, and so on. It is especially annoying when none of these characters are ever fleshed out. This is very true with Rui as she comes off as the most clichéd type of bully imaginable who is angry all the time for no real reason. The Sachi character really should have been developed more considering the whole quirk of the game is her character. Aside from her appearance, her unique characteristic of being a cyclops has almost no bearing on the story at all. She could have been depicted as a normal person with two eyes and the exact same character traits and the story could have played out the same. It is just a major disappointment to not see this aspect used at all.
And that brings me to the other major problem with the game: the story. All in all, it is a very predictable high school romance story. The player-character meets a cute girl, they spend time together, go on dates, and be happy. I really do not think I am spoiling anything here. Nothing of substance happens in the story. There are no plot twists, no major developments. Even considering the short length of the game, this was a chore to complete.
Alas, even the music itself is not that great. It quickly became repetitive and irritating.
There is one other aspect that I must comment on. In the bonus content that is unlocked after completing the game, the creator is pretty open about the fact that some of his fetishes (he mentions eating and scars) made their way into the game. A few scenes in the game depict Mamoru touching Sachi's various scars which was awkward enough during play, but knowing the creator's intentions just gives the scenes even more negative connotations. Is it really necessary to depict a girl with injuries just to satisfy some weird fetish? This type of writing is really inexcusable and should have been left out.
Overall, this game is a disappointment. Though the artwork is pretty good, the other major aspects of this game totally failed with a boring and predictable story and clichéd and forgettable characters. This game is definitely not worth the full asking price of $9.99. I bought it 75% off during the summer sale and I am not sure if it is even worth that considering the short length. I am honestly not sure whom I would recommend this to other than maybe visual novel fanatics who want a cheap game on sale.

First of all, a warning about the foul language in this game: This game has a lot of it. More f words than I hear in an average month IRL - would definitely get an R rating as a movie for language alone.
However, if that doesn't offend you or you're willing to deal with it to enjoy a free game, then this might be worth your time. (And there's not much else to warn you about except the average thrilling/scary moment here and there.)
Pros:
- The price is right.
- Unique, interesting story
- Unique gameplay
- Puzzles
- Diverse settings - the Park is especially beautiful despite the simplicity of the exterior and skybox.
- Simple inventory and abilities setup. If you need to do something new, text appears to tell you what you can do and how to do it as you approach the location.
Cons:
- Some puzzles depend on noticing arbitrary details, trying random stuff, or trying things multiple times. Good logic won't work on its own. (Could be a pro for some, I guess).
- A couple jumps that take precision key pressing. Miss and you get to restart the level/section.
- Saving progress requires pausing the game to note the section title/password. There's no other way to continue where you left off. (I recommend looking at the pause screen regularly!)
- "Fantastic" graphics setting is somewhat optimisticly named. Objects always looks boxy, but the lighting and texturing are pretty good.
- Sound is not very well localized at times. Things you say as the protagonist can't always be heard depending on where you are and sounds don't carry across distance very well - even in small rooms you can't always hear the radio that's loud when you're standing next to it.
- Most of the enjoyment of the story comes upon hearing the conclusion. It quickly gets tiring and somewhat depressing until then. (Could have used less talking - especially swearing - between sections.)
Overall: It's a great value for the price. Especially if you like unique, offbeat, puzzles, or all of the above.

As most people already wrote, I'm also getting tired of fancy updates with few "improvements" no one really wants or needs. FM needs an urgent re-vamp. I buy it every year, and while this year I was slightly hesitating, I bought it and - regretted.
Here are my reasons.
a) I've been following "the wishlists" for a quite few years now and the meaningful stuff people suggest (and there are wonderful and very doable ideas) hardly makes into the products.
b) opposite to previous, insignificant stuff like "social feed" always happens, and personally, I find it as painful as pre- and post- media conferences. Here is why. Simply, you won a game: there's a few "feeds" about enthusiastic fans and always  one claiming "messi wasn't anything special". In other words, although it was added to help realism of the game, it really doesn't matter how did your team play, you always get pretty same (or very similar) "feeds".
c) Academies! Academies! Academies! At this point, I find "youth intake" which you cannot influence at all - no matter what they claim - quite irritating. It hardly changed since 97/98. In reality, you don't have any control over it. I find it impossible if your club has the state-of-art facilites, extensive recruitment, throphy after throphy and it's absolutely focused on youth development that your 'youth intake' is absolutely worthless. Don't get me wrong, I do not expect a Messi or Ronaldo every year, but if your club reaches worldwide reputiation (and it's focued on youth development), I do expect at least several or perhaps few average players each year. Moreover, I personally find getting a good player to develop keeps my interest on the game.
d) Facilities! Ok, I'm not talking about graphics. I believe a lot of people play in 2D anyway. I'm talking something more specific than "improve facilities" and waiting until October or December in the game for facilites to actually be improved. I'm pretty sure there are little improvements each club can do on its facilities (replace seats, install under-soli heating, invest in office-space...) which can come handy and also get more related with getting better sponsorship, sales of goods during the game...
e) Dynamic rivalries! There has been a lot of talk about it, so I'll explain what I precisely mean. If one club in the league starts doing outstanding in continental competition, I find it ridiculous that its league rivals after 2, 5, 10 years of losing cannot 'follow the example' for improvement, find external funding, change owner...Especially, when today this is very dynamic everywhere and it would also add interest to the game. Now, we have something as so-and-so bought a club, they want to take it to the new heights and then ______________Or in other words, nothing happens.
Long story short, I'm not buying game next year if I get bunch of 'rearranged stat tools' and another fancy update.

I see a lot of people comparing this to Civ V, and I can undertand why, turn based 4X strategy. However I think that Endless Legend really stands up to Civ in its own right. It is certainly a hell of a lot prettier and at times a lot more challenging. The diversity of the races is absolutely a plus, each with amazing pros and intimidating cons. And the district system which Civ VI is stealing is definitely a much more accurate and interesting method of controlling city growth, and the army/unit stacking system is certainly a load more appealing than Civ V's single unit per tile policy and it can speed up turns signicantly. With a greater emphasis on planning and micromanagement, and an actual story for each faction and lore behind the game, I think that Endless Legend cannot really be compared to Civ; although it's the same genre, it has many mechanics that just work a lot better, it's more colourful, more challenging, less dry and simple; it lets you really get down to the nitty gritty of manging everything yourself, and I totally understand that that isn't everyone's idea of a great experience, but for me, this is a fantastic strategy game, that ALL devs can learn from, even 2K apparently.

This game is Civilization V's older, smarter, and frankly, sexier sibling. The aesthetic is gorgeous, the gameplay (especially combat) is far more unique and interesting, winter is coming, and factions play drastically different from one another. It has a steeper learning curve (which is in my opinion the reason for all the negative reviews in the last week or so), and games will generally go a lot faster than your average Civ V campaign, usually reigning in between turns 150 - 200.
There are a great many options before starting a game that you should take a look at, most notably the map generation tools, which offer a great level of customization; altitude, ocean size, continents, resource sparsity, and # of minor factions are just a fraction of the things you can mess with.
One of the things I STRONGLY recommend doing before starting a campaign is setting the combat speed to as fast as possible, lest your combat sequences end up taking 2 - 4x as long just because you're watching tedious running/combat animations.
A potential downside from a player standpoint is that this game requires a LOT of min-maxing to play effectively. This means rotating populations in each city from working on food one turn, to gold the next, to production or science after--I don't mind this so much, but I can see how it can become annoying, especially in a multiplayer setting or later in the campaign when you have tons of cities.
If you're looking for an immersive, fresh take on the 4X fantasy genre with some fresh ideas and very well-thought out game design, then I strongly recommend buying this game. The game is worth buying for the full price, but if you can get this game of under $20, it's a steal. As for DLC, I don't own any of it, but I will eventually pick it up on sale, and I'd recommend you do the same.

First off any negetive review soley based on the fact this is NOT FFO, all I can say is learn to read.  While I am not entirely sure what this "App" is doing on Steam (Though they have a lot of things that shouldnt be on steam now), they are very clear on the what this is.
This is making an account to reserve your name now and an information hub that the more you use the more "Brownie Points" you earn.  The BP are used for FFO in game currency .. it does not say if it is regular or bought with cash currency but either way you are not paying to earn BP if you want to.
The Big Damn Hero package, for $5, adds a special quest which will showcase a statue of you in a town which others can see.  To some people that is already worth it.  You also get access to the Verse map and trading game.  Essentially point and click for trivia information on each planet/moon.  While doing trade runs a character from the show will ask you to go to a certain planet/moon that you need to find (They give you directions so its not hard, and you can click on hint which costs you some time off your run but adds a pulsating glow around your target).  There is a daily and weekly run for chest rewards, and a basic practice run that is untimed and gives you 50 BP each go that you can do as much as you like.  The chests contain cards (and BP) which you collect for FFO digital items and if you get extras you can trade them in for more BP.  You can also buy card packs if you choose for a couple bucks that is a seperate purchase from Big Damn Hero perks (You can buy the packs regardless of buying Big Damn Hero).
So basically if you want to call this a money grab fine.  What developer isnt trying to earn money and gauge interest?  The difference here is they are very specific on what you get without being sketchy at all .. everything they say this is before any spending and promise you IF you spend is delivered with the obvious exception of anything you do now towards FFO in game rewards is subject to the game actually coming out. The Cortex may not be sprawling with content at the moment, but it serves as a neat little app to build up my excitement for the final game and get ready with some extra stuff to be redeemed once I start playing. The 5$ price for full access to the whole thing may seem like a quick money-grab to some, but I'm happily giving away money that I'd otherwise spend on a meal at Burger King to help these devs make a dream come true.
It's a small amount to pay for what has the potential to be great, and judging from what I've seen and heard from the devs, they seem to know what they're doing. They've made it very clear that no one should have an advantage by paying money, and they seem to have a genuine love for the show. And if that isn't enough to convince you, they have all the main actors on board for the game.
For those who are a little frustrated about the nature of the micro-transactions, I urge you all to check out the podcast on The Signal, which is linked in the Cortex. I trust these developers, and I'm happy to support them. Here's to a great release of Firefly Online!

Pay no heed to most negative reviews. The software gives exactly what it proposed:
BASIC VOCABULARY and PRONUNCIATION.
As such, it doesn't teach verbs and grammar, so it is a HELPER program for someone already studying a language and for children.
I am a teacher, and I can already say this program would be pretty nice for children's earlier years... Definitely better than children books of basic vocabulary due to its interactivity, and also cheaper than most similar books. (I wonder if there's a way to corporate-buy 30 copies of the software...)

Use this alongside a proper language learning course. It is best suited for languages that don't have gendered nouns (e.g. English) and simple pluralization rules (or a lack of plural forms altogether). It's definitely worth its cheap price, even more so if you grab it in a sale. This is also not a game for which you need to own all the DLC to get the full gameplay experience.
I think this is a great way to learn words, as you hear the pronunciation, read the spelling, and see the object in question at the same time.
This game will only help you learn vocabulary, and this is mostly limited to nouns for objects found in the house. This is not a language course you can use stand-alone, but a learning tool to be used alongside others.
I only own the German language pack, and I really wish the voice pronouncing all the words would also include the definite article (words like der/die/das). Plural forms would also be nice, as German has relatively complex rules for pluralizing nouns, which also change depending on the noun's gender.

Yes... this "installment" of Metal Gear Solid (some might not even call it that) may not be the fully fleshed-out, fifth chapter in the MGS saga that we were hoping for, but that's not at all what this game looks to accomplish. Ground Zeroes serves as a narrative prologue, a tease at what sort of epic, stealth-oriented action we can expect from The Phantom Pain when it comes out later this year (September 1, if all goes well). Boy oh boy... well it's got me excited! Having NEVER played MGS, this was a very welcome introduction to the franchise. I couldn't quite follow the story (as expected), but, nonetheless, for what this game aims to do, MGS Ground Zeroes is a great game. The intense rescue missions and compelling cover based fire fights were intense and engaging. Landing a silent take down or a risky head shot from afar was oh, so satisfying. SNAKE IS A TOTAL BAD♥♥♥♥♥ Visually, this game is absolutely gorgeous and greatly optimized for the PC, which was the icing on the cake. Some may argue that the game is far too short for it's initial asking price of $30 when it first launched and I'm inclined to agree. However, to my surprise, I found a decent amount of re-playability as there are multiple tactics and methods to be used and choices to be made while tackling a particular mission. Now that the game is a mere $10, do not hesitate.

I can recommend this game, because it really is just a prologue to the upcoming Phantom Pain in which I found extremely entertaining, but keep in mind it is not ideal for PC enthusists. Though, what I can say without spoiling anything, is that this game prologue is extremely short. It has one mission in which you can tackle in a few different ways. The "Hard" difficulty and some Spec-Op missions are unlocked after one playthrough, but playtime averages only from 1 to 2 hours total.
Also, Ground Zeroes is a PS4 port. This means it has been tailored for the PC directly from the PS4 without optimizations, aside from graphical optimizations. This PC version does have enhanced visuals, but the game constantly makes it obvious that it does not want you to play with keyboard and mouse, rather than a gamepad. Menus must be operated with the keyboard alone, if not the gamepad, but gameplay is not bad at all whilst using the gamepad. Another thing is that the frames-per-second has been capped to 60. PC enthusists would probably want the option to go to 120 and I personally can live with as low as 90, but 60 is just an insult. If we have the technology, at least give us the option.
The PC version of Phantom Pain will probably be a PS4 port as well, given Sony has some under-the-table deals with the Metal Gear Solid series, so I'd expect some of the same issues. Though, I will probably still purchase Phantom Pain, because of the immersive graphics, innovative advanced AI and the fun factor. If Ground Zeroes has done anything for me, it definitely got me hyped up for Phantom Pain, as it opened the doors on the heavy, intense plot that is about to unfold.
I'd recommend this prologue for if the price tag is somewhere under $20, but if not, I'm sure Phantom Pain will provide at least some backstory.

I looked through a lot of reviews before writing this and I find myself in a quandry. I can understand both the positive and negative reviews I read, they are mostly coherent and true. I have played most of the 4x games(historical, fantasy and sci-fi) that have ever been published so I think I can reasonably say I am speaking from experience.
Positives
I have played over 1400 hours including all the expansions. With that said I obviously like the game and I don't think I have anything new to say that you can't already read in other reviews.
Negatives
There are still some things that bug me about the game even after several expansions and updates and I think they deserve mentioning. I have noticed that people that like this game are almost defensive about it and refuse to admit it's weaknesses.
Documentation, rules, tutorials - These are all pretty bad especially for a game that many people would find complex. I really enjoy games with depth to them, that is not what I am talking about. Even after 1400 hours their are technical elements of the game I do not understand and rules I am surprised by. That shouldn't happen (especially with an experienced gamer). Much of the useful documentation has been published by players. I find it frustrating to dig through home made guides that may or may not answer my questions. The discussion group can be equally opaque. Hoping you can guess the right key word that will take you to a comment applicable  to your issue is equally frustrating. Just as a prime example, the game has several races you can play. There was 1 race in particular that I just wasn't understanding fully despite a variety of searches. At one point someone suggested a tutorial on YouTube. I clicked the link, it was just under an hour long!? And, no I did not even try to watch it.
Combat - In a way this goes with my previous comment. Despite my research I still don't think I fully understand the manual combat. You give your units some generalized commands(order matters) and hope they do what you asked of them. Some of the behavior the units perform is thoroughly bewildering, i.e. you tell a unit to 'Defend' and it charges forward? Regardless, it is a long game and between that and the peculiarities of combat I simply use autocombat barring some unusual circumstances. Personally I enjoy empire building over tactics, but that is just a matter of taste.
Bugs - despite how long it's been out there are still several bugs. Are they game stoppers, generally no, that doesn't mean that I enjoy them. The developers have offered many updates and you are welcome to post bugs on their site as long as you have a save file to go with it. Not all bugs can be demonstrated with a save file.
In the end, do I recommend the game, absolutely, but it has it's flaws.

Endless legend is one of the games I watched while I was computerless until recently, (the horror!) I was very interested in the setting and the feel of the game. In this it does not disappoint, and it also doesnt disappoint as 4x game well at least for the first 3 x's the Explore is fantastic the world is beutiful and full of minor anomolies that put any of Civ 5's natural wonders to shame. The Expand is unique with both the normal base building and the ability to assimilate neutral factions into your empire. Exploit is handled differently then civ rather then build on tiles with workers your cities can expand into certain tiles specifically giving you access to more resources and territory, and finally Exterminate and this is unfortunetly where the game falls flat.
I've always enjoyed ALL four x's in a 4x game so Im not just some kill! burn! command and conquer player, okay I am that but I enjoy when a game covers all the bases. In Endless Legend you have units that you can upgrade with certain equipment which can grant a variety of improvements or even counter other unit types. The actual combat itself isn't bad you make armies and then they fight on a smaller map in what is very like Civ 5 and you can give them specific orders or even move them onto hills or out of danger.

As most people already wrote, I'm also getting tired of fancy updates with few "improvements" no one really wants or needs. FM needs an urgent re-vamp. I buy it every year, and while this year I was slightly hesitating, I bought it and - regretted.
Here are my reasons.
a) I've been following "the wishlists" for a quite few years now and the meaningful stuff people suggest (and there are wonderful and very doable ideas) hardly makes into the products.
b) opposite to previous, insignificant stuff like "social feed" always happens, and personally, I find it as painful as pre- and post- media conferences. Here is why. Simply, you won a game: there's a few "feeds" about enthusiastic fans and always  one claiming "messi wasn't anything special". In other words, although it was added to help realism of the game, it really doesn't matter how did your team play, you always get pretty same (or very similar) "feeds".
c) Academies! Academies! Academies! At this point, I find "youth intake" which you cannot influence at all - no matter what they claim - quite irritating. It hardly changed since 97/98. In reality, you don't have any control over it. I find it impossible if your club has the state-of-art facilites, extensive recruitment, throphy after throphy and it's absolutely focused on youth development that your 'youth intake' is absolutely worthless. Don't get me wrong, I do not expect a Messi or Ronaldo every year, but if your club reaches worldwide reputiation (and it's focued on youth development), I do expect at least several or perhaps few average players each year. Moreover, I personally find getting a good player to develop keeps my interest on the game.
d) Facilities! Ok, I'm not talking about graphics. I believe a lot of people play in 2D anyway. I'm talking something more specific than "improve facilities" and waiting until October or December in the game for facilites to actually be improved. I'm pretty sure there are little improvements each club can do on its facilities (replace seats, install under-soli heating, invest in office-space...) which can come handy and also get more related with getting better sponsorship, sales of goods during the game...
e) Dynamic rivalries! There has been a lot of talk about it, so I'll explain what I precisely mean. If one club in the league starts doing outstanding in continental competition, I find it ridiculous that its league rivals after 2, 5, 10 years of losing cannot 'follow the example' for improvement, find external funding, change owner...Especially, when today this is very dynamic everywhere and it would also add interest to the game. Now, we have something as so-and-so bought a club, they want to take it to the new heights and then ______________Or in other words, nothing happens.
Long story short, I'm not buying game next year if I get bunch of 'rearranged stat tools' and another fancy update.

Port Quality
Absolutely worth the money on PC, especially if you can grab it on sale. Graphics quality scales nicely, and every visual enhancement works in the game's favor. Only technical downside is the game isnt fully optimized for keyboard and mouse, though you either get used to it, or use a controller. For the first MGS game on PC in a while, Kojima Productions has done a phenomenal job.
Gameplay
One of the best open world games on PC simply because the stealth mechanics work so well. Of course, the entire game itself takes place in one, fairly open air level. What that means is a lot of tagging guards and taking them out. This is essentially the grind of the game, but the AI is robust and varied, so there are many approaches to even just disabling an enemy and it never gets boring. This is good, as there are only 7 missions, most of which dont take longer than an hour (if you're bad) to complete. These missions have varied objectives, from assassinating targets to extracting prisoners, and the only way to get the highest ranks is to be stealthy. If stealthing isnt your thing, there is still a lot of fun to be had in using deadlier methods, and those techniques have their own variations as well. The fact is that there is a lot of hours of gameplay, but you have to be willing to explore these styles of play, and really have to want to play missions again and again to get the highest ranks, not necessarily 100% the game (like me) but to try missions a different way each time.
Story
Not as cerebral or involved, plot wise, but still has good character development and twists. A downside to this is that most of the story is told through casette tapes, so you have to be really interested in the MGS backstory to listen to the tapes from this game, and from MGS Peacewalker, which are included. Because of this there are no classic MGS codec conversations, which is a bummer. Another let down is that Snake hardly talks at all in this game, everything is told at him and he hardly has repsonses for what is going on, other than a constant scowl on his face. Which is appropriate considering the completely horrifying situation his comrades are facing at the hands of the new villain. MGS is taking a more serious tone here, and its not only in the name of making light of terrible situations that happen in warfare, but it also gives the characters and story depth that is really engaging on another level.
I do think some of it will go too far for some people, especially those who look to MGS to be their slapstick, goofy military tropes game, as a breather from all these super-hardcore modern military shooters (whose stories are only for the most intellectual and serious of adults, amirite?). For those people, this story will rub them the wrong way, but if they never treated the MGS story as serious in the first place, they don't really deserve to be angry or bewildered that the story they never cared about is trying to make a story in a videogame be taken seriously.

Best RTS I've ever played for those who enjoy combat AND resource management. I've re-bought this game three times, including the HD remaster on Steam, and I still play it with my brother every now and then. I'm a bit biased due to my emotional connection to the game over the years but I know the game very well by this point.
For a game nowadays, the graphics leave something to be desired for sure; however, I can honestly say that it doesn't bother me that much after getting into it. Single Player skirmishes get boring, because you eventually figure out the AI patterns and can exploit them for easy wins. Despite this, Single player campaigns and scenarios are fun, very challenging and do a thorough job of teaching you all the important parts of gameplay, while also giving you a small taste of actual real world history (if you're into that sort of thing.) You can also just build your own castles and levels and make your own maps. As a single player purchase, I'd still say the current $2.49 price is well worth what you get.
In addition to the single player content, there is online or LAN multiplayer (yes people still play it online -- get GameRanger) where you can engage in strategic, resource based combat with a friend or a player online. If you like extensive resource driven RTS's with solid tactical combat then this is the game for you.
Where Stronghold: Crusader (HD) shines is in its level of micromanagement; everything matters in a game in Stronghold: Crusader from where you put your granary to how much you tax your people and where you position your archers. Destroying your enemies supply chains is just as, if not more important, than direct assaults and there are many nuanced features In this game such as wall scaling, tunneling, burning oil and fire propagation which keep can keep a match interesting. This level of controlled micromanagement may be a deterrent for those RTS players who might feel overloaded by having to constantly think and move. However, if you want an engaging competitive or cooperative experience where you need to utilize thought and reflexes to succeed then Crusader has you covered, buy a copy for you and some friends and have the best LAN RTS experience of your life.

I had the highest of hopes for Lego Batman 3. I love lego and the DC Universe and Lego Batman 2 was one of my favourite games of 2012. I had completed the first game to 100% and it was fairly by the numbers for a lego game, hub area and missions branching off of that, the thing I really enjoyed was the villain storyline, noticably absent from subsequent releases. Anyhow, trailers for Lego Batman 2: DC heroes unite hit the internet and I was super hyped, with promises of heroes from other DC books including the flash, green lantern and superman. I bought the game and it delivered in spades, but what I didn't know I wanted was the amazing open world hub of Gotham city, now obviously it was scaled down but it was all there, arkham asylum, ace chemicals, and nothing could beat the feeling of getting a mission and racing to arkham in the batmobile, or running through the city at ridiculous speeds as the flash, and flying with the old superman theme blasting away was absolutely stunning. My two gripes were however, even though we saw metropolis, it was not available for roaming around in and the other dc heroes apart from superman were introduced late and kind of an afterthought, but it didn't matter because I could fight crime as them in the open world. Inbetween the release of lego batman 2 and 3 there was an amazing game by the name of Lego Marvel Super Heroes, and I am less of a fan of the marvel stuff but it was incredible, new york city was huge with the baxter building and the sheild hellicarrier available to fly to or jump from. "Okay" I thought, "how are Lego gonna up the anti in the new Lego Batman game?" "What's the subtitle again?" Beyond Gotham, In my head this was going to be what Lego Marvel was but the helicarrier was the watchtower and we could have metropolis and coast city. But no. I bought the game on a sale as I didn't have the money on release, I played the story to the point where I could return to watchtower, and was dissapointed. "Okay" I thought "I'll just beat the game and then we can see what we unlock" not a single city is what. No patrolling gotham to kill time, no flying over in the batwing or chilling in the batcave before rushing through the secret door to the rescue. You can now access the suits anywhere by holding Y, now in theory I see this working for overworld fun, instead of having to place suits everywhere, you can just change on the go. But it doesn't work because batman with a jetpack is amazing in gotham city but boring in the hall of justice, so all it does is force the suits to require these charging stations which limit your use of batman with a jetpack in order to make the puzzles less easily solvable,  this creates a "you can't tell me what to do feel" toward the game because you have the suit, the game just won't let you use it. The writing is stupid save for some admittedly funny lines, braniac is not in the least intimidating and sounds like an annoying idiot who likes collecting things rather than the calm calculating evil mastermind he should be. Apparently batman thinks heroes shouldn't have emotions which is stupid for so many reasons but mainly because his emotion of greif for his parents' deaths and his love for the city and not wanting anyone to go through what he did, he becomes the batman. Don't buy this game, if you haven't played Lego Batman 2, go and buy it instead and if you have play Lego Marvel and if you have played both wait for lego batman 4 or lego marvel 2 because this one really isn't worth your money.

This game... is unique. I'll certainly grant it that. Pretty much unlike any other game I've played, and I've played some weird ones. It's not a walking sim, a horror game, or an adventure game, but it does borrow from all of these genres. It's annoying and frustrating and certainly very confusing, but it's also hilarious and charming, which is why I've decided to recommend it.
PROS:
-Voice acting is great and as believable as can be for some of these absurdist situations
-Game looks surpisingly beautiful, especially in some of the outdoor scenes
-Very original gameplay most of the time
-Intersting plot
CONS:
-Plot is downright confusing and obtuse. I like picking things apart like this, so I didn't mind it, but some might
-It's a bit buggy. I couldn't walk normally up certain staircases and had to sprint/jump, for example
-It is difficult. This game will not remind you of your objectives; it expects you to be smart enough to just figure stuff out from hints and riddles
-The gun mechanics in a section or twoare pretty bad. It's quite difficult to see where you're aiming, even when you right click
Overall, I'd say give it a go, especially if you're into absurdist works or finding obscure anime easter eggs (there are a few in this game). It's definitely a game you'll remember for a long time if you find your way to the end. And, best of all, it's free and will only take up a few hours of your time.

Well-made, but not quite to the point where I don't regret spending 10 dollars. As said in other reviews, this is basically an interactive flashcard program. Everything is very high-quality, but it needs more substance. Had I checked the reviews, I would gladly have paid $5 for this someday.
It's very well-made, and a lot of work must have gone towards acquiring the very good audio samples (I tried it in Russian). The developer has replied to some of the more popular (and angsty) reviews, but I hope he/she can respond to the more constructive ones as well. One assumes when looking at a "language game" that it will help build their language skills, rather than just vocabulary. I don't think there's very much demand for that, however.
I sincerely hope they can rework this game to be more about building functionality for players, allowing them gain at least a basic sense of sentence structure and grammar so that they can put these words to use. I had hoped to find something more along the lines of a gameified Rosetta Stone. As a former ESL teacher, I had hoped that someone did what I would like to do some day--find a way to teach foreign languages in a gaming setting. These guys have taken a great first step, but all I can do is find myself hoping for something more.
I realize that restructuring this game to be a more comprehensive language tool would mean a *LOT* of work. For a game that did what most negative reviewers (and I) hoped, I would happily pay more like $20-$30. Currently toying with the idea of asking for a refund, but I may let them keep my $10 unhindered in the hope that the game will see radical updates someday.

By this point, reviewing Football Manager becomes more of a review of the series than a review of each individual game. FM has really begin to stagnate over the last several years; personally, I don't feel as if any game changing introductions have been made since FM13.
Yet, when you remove the rose-tinted glasses of previous installments, it's hard to say that FM17 is anything other than a genre leading game.
It's worth noting that several of the negative reviews on here do have some strong foundations. The match engine is very 'spontaneous' in its creation of highlights, as a result leaving AI players making the most unbelievable of decisons, and it's hard to deny that press conferences and interviews are anything other than a tedious grind that becomes the bane of your life after several hours of gameplay.
However, the fundamental elements of gameplay are strong and allow for players to sink copious amounts of hours into generating wonderkids that are found in deepest darkest Peru, developing their own pub team into world beating superstars and winning the Premier League with Liverpool.
Download the demo if doubtful, but FM17 is, although a small step forward, a step forward none the less.

New to Metal Gear? Might as well start with this. Do you have to?
Well you could wait until other Metal Gear games or Konami somehow reaches the PC, much like Capcom. Or you can start new and fresh with this short prequel of the upcoming blockbuster game of 2015 just to familiarize controls. That's also enough time to catch up on the story of the series so far if you really are into that.
What you will find is "Next generation" refinement no other developer has ever done before. Somehow the game, no matter how hectic. No matter how complex the Ai pathing, protocol, and combat tactics. No matter how many explosions happen on screen and in the real time cinematic that uses the same models and environments that are featured in the actual gameplay. The game maintains the standard 60 frames per second that other "Next Generation" developers are ether unable or too lazy to do. All on a high performance computer with late last generation hardware, or what I would call a PS4.
This is only achieved by the lack of detailed environmental oscillation, or the fact that every strand of grass does not have to be shaded with its own individual defining shadow from said light source. Sadly real life is not under an intense lamp as a form of sunlight, and every open field does not have such lamps shining intense light that defines the artistic merit of such blades of grass things. That would be too many lamps, and think of those lamps as being powered by your computer hardware. That means this game has truly one light emitting source or the models themselves do not have their own individual light sources when light supposedly shines on them (oldschool lighting).
OR somehow rendering has become so advanced that there is no need to render anything behind an object or off camera? You don’t actually see the object, it is to question of the object is actually there. But what if you heard a sound nearby in the environment? Usually the sound source is when you are nearby the actual model of that object? Usually the game slows down when there is such a sound source, as it is an active fully rendered model that has physical presence on the environmental plain even though it is unseen by the camera.
What if the entire level was not pre-rendered and it only renders things actively when they are shown on the screen, your camera view? Is this the true power of mainstream “Next Generation”?
No other $20 game will offer you that.

ARK: Survival Of The Fittest is basically a jurassic Hunger Games. You can choose to play alone in Free-For-All, or play with up to 3 others in 4-man tribes. This game has a small learning curve, but once you get the hang of it, it's a very fun game!
-

These dinosaurs help you carry more items, and attack enemies for you. These dinosaurs typically deal more damage and have higher health than you, so it's definitely recommended to tame more than one.
-
The graphics in this game are very nice to look at and are very detailed. Sometimes, in the midst of the chaos, it's nice just to take in the scenery around you. The world was very beautifully designed.
-
This game takes character creation to a whole new level. Not only can you choose the basic stuff: hair color, eye color, size of your character, gender, etc., but you can also over-exaggerate these features like crazy! If you wanted to, you could make a character that is 4 feet tall with very muscular arms and very skinny chicken legs, and so much more!
-
This game is kind of poorly optimised. If you want this game to run smooth (or over 30 FPS), you must use a good graphics card.
-
If you've played ARK: Survival Evolved, this most likely won't be a problem for you. But, if you were like me and just started off with this game, it is certainly a challenge when you're first learning how to play this game. Learning how to tame dinosaurs, how to get good loot, and how to use some weapons can be a challenge. Just be prepared to face players with more skill than you, and be patient. You will learn how to win, it's not too hard!
-
Evolution Events are random events that occur that are specifically designed to endanger the player (with the exception of a few events: Double Taming, Food of the Gods, Harvest Bounty, Herbivore Drop, Supply Overload, Super Loot Crate). Some Evolution Events, such as Mega Heat, are kind of broken. For example, with Mega Heat, the player must remove all of their clothes to help cool off. This wouldn't be such a problem if the Event didn't maintain that heat. You could even swim in the river and constantly drink but still lose health due to the heat. Of course, these aren't big issues, just be careful when the events occur!
This game is very fun. It has awesome graphics, as well as an amazing atmosphere. It gives you the ability to tame dinosaurs and create silly characters. Although, you will not be able to run this game smoothly unless you have a good graphics card. The learning curve is a challenge to get used to, but isn't too big of an issue. The Evolution Events are designed to kill you, and are very good at doing their job.

I'm happy to play games with surrealistic stories or plots, and I'm happy to play games with interesting mechanics. Only If has none of those things - it just doesn't make any sense.
Here's a brief rundown of the first 10 minutes of the game:
(1) Cutscene where I walk into a house party
(2) Warped to a magically dark environment, have to chase a light through a maze
(3) Listen to an Italian guy curse at me while objects move around an entirely different room
(4) Time challenge to find a key that magically appeared in the house with no clues
(5) Warp to a different room, pick up a chess piece, solve a simple puzzle, die?
(6) Wait I'm not dead? Press Space to swim (literally)
(7) Get shot in awful stealth puzzle, respawn and try again
(8) Press E to... do something? I didn't fast enough and it respawned me back at (6). More "press Space to swim!"
At this point I literally have no idea how to even interact with this game, so I give up.
The fatal failing of Only If is that the player is never grounded in the experience of playing the game. A movie plays by itself, but a game requires players to complete certain actions to move forward. I can't say if the story is good or bad because I can't actually understand the game enough to move forward. It's artificially difficult to even attempt to interact with the game.
I will say that this game is profoundly bad enough to encourage me to write a review of it, warning others to stay away. So I guess Only If has managed to elicit a strong emotional reaction after all. But I doubt it's what the creators wanted.

Endless Legend is perhaps the best Civ-like game I've played.  Mostly because of the gorgeous environments, the interesting races, and the multitude of things to discover.  The races play extremely differently from one another, which gives the game far more replayabilty than Civ in which the differences are so minor that you would do fine even if you didn't look up your race's special ability.  Also, there is more of a focus on adventuring, kind of like Age of Wonders, so you are never left just clicking end turn over and over again while you wait for your human opponents to wage interminably long wars.  Finally city management is more interesting with it allowing you to put your citizens to work in different ways.
My only complaint is the wonky combat system which makes perhaps too many choices for you, but it is interesting too, I think of myself as more of a general while my troops do what they think is best.

A fantastic, deep, engaging 4X game.
A good 4X is really hard to pull off well, and few manage to hit all the notes required. In that regard, Endless Legends is a symphony.

In Endless Legend, you lead one of the major factions of Auriga. Auriga is dying, from millenia of abuse and destruction, and it is up to your faction and it's vision to shape the planet and avoid the impending cataclysm.
Personal Rating: 9/10
Pros:
+Complex, deep gameplay
+Actual storylines
+10/10 artstyle and music
+Completely moddable
+Well-crafted fantasy setting (I love the lore of the Endless.)
+Cool UI
Cons:
-Sometimes too complex; too many things can be going on at later turns
-Steep learning curve
-Quests and storylines can feel restrictive
Endless Legend is one the most complicated 4x titles out there. It's not a game you can run on autopilot skipping every turn and just racking up the resources to quickbuy your win condition. You have to actually get off the throne and do stuff outside of your territory; you can't just turtle within your borders and expect the AI to respect you. You have to actually properly equip your armies if you want to win battles, and you have to actually care about and predict the actions and win conditions of the other empires.
Yes, victory will mostly depend on min-maxing what you have. That's how battles are won, with careful attention and strategy. No thumb-twiddling, turn-skipping. The AI can be very smart at times, and they notice what win conditions you're gunning for.
All in all, get it if you're into grand lore and lovely space fantasy, and if you like a complex and demanding 4x experience.

Endless Depth.  Endless Complexity.  Endless Customization.  Endless Confusion.  Endless Timesink.  I've got pages of these.
Stand Out Features: All the 4x turn based gaming you know and love, now with questing, customizable races with customizable army units and a narrative mission embedded into each race to vary up their gameplay and help them stand out among the others.  Changing seasons force adaptation.  Battles between units are micromangaged and take place on the world map, allowing players to maximize the effectiveness of their unit compositions and terrain.
Pros: Extreme levels of customization.  Multiple viable paths to victory.  Racial quests and traits make all factions feel vastly different from one another.  Combat minigame allows for intelligent and tactical army compositions.  Mulityplayer support in a 4x game.  Writing and the overall world lore are fascinating and novel-esk.  Art and music sell the ambiance of the high fantasy, alien world.
Cons: Complicated game (lots of passive traits and stats to juggle for cities, armies, and factions, both your stats and the stats of your opponents).  Amount of text in quests and story gets overwhelming.  Tactical battles slow down multiplayer games and get tedious overall after a while.  Lacks the polish of comparable 4x triple A games (to be expected, but true nevertheless).
Would Recommend To: Civilization 4 fans looking for something a bit more complicated.  4X fans with lots of free time and patience.  Endless Space fans who want more of that Endless Space experience.
Would Alternatively Suggest: Civilization 5 with expansions (Brave New World at least) to those looking for the same overall experience without so much crunch.  XCom/XCom 2 for players looking for a more fleshed out tactical game experience and are willing to abandon the civilization development theme.  Endless Space for people craving all the Pros listed above for about the same price point and a touch less complexity.
--I'm mixed on this one.  Will thumbs up it ultimately because despite its flaws, its a remarkably well thought out game, but if you want something more streamlined, consider any of my alternate suggestions.

What I really like, is although the general idea is just a sort of cut and paste sentence builder,
a few layers of strategy are built in.
Combos can be built by repeatedly mentioning the same subject, each character has subjects
they are particularly sensitive to, (which you can exploit given the chance) and you can use select
"wildcards" your opponent can't see.
You also grab the components of your sentences/insults taking turns with your opponent from the same pile, meaning
if you pay attention, you can try to predict what subject they will use or what they are going to try to build. So you can quickly adjust if possible by taking something they'd need for example.
All of this creates a very "board game" feel to it, and makes it shine.
Especially with the humor and the fact that insults can sound pretty funny when they don't make sense, but can still be played because the phrase is still grammatically correct.
Throw in some "classy" voices, and classical music, and you're in for some smiles.
You can play against the CPU, "Hot-Seat Style", or online vs friends or random opponents.

This game is fantastic.
On the surface it seems like a simple, stupid piece of fun .. but things get a bit deeper when you play online against real humans. It's actually a pretty deep turn based strategy/card game at it's core. You won't see much challenging game play vs the AI who always seems to spout nonsense insults that amount to little to nothing. Playing online however you face off against players who actually know how to play and string together insult combo's that require you to out-think your opponent.
Do you take the continuation? Can your opponent get more than 15 points to cancel you? Should you cop a grammar penalty to take the last "is a cheese shop" card and break your opponents combo? There is an incredible amount of depth to this game that just seems like simple stupid fun.
The downside is that there are a lot of idiot's online who disconnect rather than take a loss, which can be annoying. But that's a pretty common problem in any online 1v1 environment even in AAA titles, for an indie dev I can hardly blame them for that. They are aparently working on a way to fix the issue though.
This game is a steal for 1-2$ .. I would have payed upwards of $5 easily and have gotten tonnes of enjoyment out of it.

This is a pretty good 'language learning' game, it does have some flaws, such as it not really helping with grammar or phrases, but it also is pretty useful as a vocabulary game. It's gameplay is a bit.... lacking, but it has some really good achievements. It has very humourous parts to it, as well as it's storyline.
There are few language learning games on Steam, and to be fair, this isn't really much of a 'language learning' game, sure it's a good aid for learning language, but it doesn't ahve anything to do with grammar or phrases, more of a vocabulary game. Don't get this game if you expect it to teach you an entire language, to learn a language, it's best to have many different sources, and this is a very useful source, although it is nothing on it's own. If you have started learning a language and need help with vocabulary, it's good for you, or even if you have not learnt a spot of the language, it's an okay starting point, to help you get used to the language.
The gameplay in this is limited, as you are locked in a house, and cannot escape. This is kind of a 'bottle episode' in that respect. You can go into first person and third person, you cannot jump, and you can open doors with the right mouse button (although the only door you can't open is the front door, believe me, I have tried), as well as being able to interact with other things. Being locked inside your house, with no indication of the passing of time, and with the only dislogue being you saying the names of objects to yourself, it makes it a pretty surreal game to play. You have to walk around and collect nouns, adjectives and verbs of your choosen language. There are quite a few words to collect, and it's half impossible to get them all, as there will always be something you miss. There are some pretty good achievements for this game as well, which is great incentive to learn more words. When you collect ten words you can do a quick quiz, where you can walk around while a word is on screen, and you need to find it in the room.
The story of this excuses it to not teaching you about grammar or phrases. It is about a guy who made a device that tells you what an object's name is in another language, but the idea is pirated and patented by someone else, and you need to prove that you made the device, and only you know how the device works, so if you can collect 400 words and master them, then you can prove that you made the device. I don't know if anything happens after you collect all the words, as I have one word left, and I cannot find it, but I expect that it has a funny ending, either that or nothing happens, wither way, it's worth it.
If you are learning a language or not I'd recommend this game, as it is a useful resource for learning a language, but it's also good if you're not learning one, as it never hurts to know more about other languages, it doesn't hurt to know other words for things in other languages. If you are learning a language I'd suggest you use other sites as well, such as
,
or
, but that doesn't mean you shouldn't buy this game. This games helps very much to give you a visual, an audio and a written of the words.

Ryse: Son of Rome was made in the Crytex engine so the graphics were great and the animation superb.
PERFORMANCE -  This was a major issue for me.
I am running a GTX970 with a 4.1 Ghz 6x core processor and 8 Gb of RAM.
The game automatically set everything to "normal" graphics settings (which I thought was weird).
Even with those settings, I would get substantial screen tearing and some judder but mostly in "movie scenes" with alot to render. Once in a while I would get the same problems during executions, but mostly when executing more than one enemy. I DID NOT SET EVERYTHING TO LOW SO I CANNOT SPEAK TO PERFORMANCE WITH THOSE SETTING ON MY HARDWARE.
GAMEPLAY
The mechanics are kinda cool especially if you were a fan of the God of War series (Ryse is similar but DOES NOT compare) in that you have light and heavy attacks and blocking which which you use when indicated by some kind of obvious movement or a colorful glow. I found the perk system kind of useful but the upgrade system rather limited to the point that I only upgraded when prompted by the game to do so. I have always liked QTE but this falls short of satisfactory regarding the mechanics. If you miss a button prompt, there is no consequence other than less perk points ie: damage, health, focus, and XP, which is fine other than the fact that I found myself caring little about hitting the right buttons. What "I" thing should happend is that you get 3 chances to execute your enemy. If you fail, your eemy blocks your strike and knocks you back taking some health along the way. Upon the third failure the execution is reversed and you are in turn slaughtered. just my two cents. If you want things to be challenging, choose the hardest difficulty and it might make it worth hitting the correct buttons in the Quick Time Events.
ASSETS
I am not a big complainer about many look alike characters so ill just say there are not many variatons of enemies.
The scenery is absolutely BEAUTIFUL (thank you crytek) and the water is on par with the rest of the game. Moving onto weapons. I know that in roman armies soldiers mostly stuck with one weapon and some times used staffs/pilums, but seeing how the story was so off base I dont think it would have been ad to allow for dual wielding of swords or staffs and such. Instead you are stuck with a sword and shield the whole time...which is fine I guess.
STORY
I have always been a big ROME dork, so I like any cheesy story the makes me feel like spartacus and such so I dont have any comlaints on the front other than lenght, though if it were to be longer with everything as is, it would be TOO long. there just isnt much to do other than kill Kill KILL. Basically there is about 4-8 hrs of gameplay depending on your playstyle and diffuculty choice.
SUMMARY
With all of my bickering I did enjoy the game. I really do love my burtal, murderous, carnage. SOOOoooo. no complaints there. All in all I do reccomend this game on sale(which it is now until Feb 12th for $6.79). Just try to play it in one sitting in order to keep from being too bored. I have nothing against the game, I just think the mechanics and assets needed ALOT more "polishing". I hope you have found this review helpful.

For starters let me say, THIS IS NOT A GAME!!  There, now that we have that cleared up I'll explain what it is...  What you've got here is an app in which you can support and get a few bonus things for the game Firefly Online, which is set to come out this spring.  The app is great for two types of people, if you'd like to be a supporter of the Firefly Online game and get a few in game bennies while you do so, or if your a big Firefly fan.  This app is being billed as free but there is a payed version which opens up a lot more for $5.00.  So lets look at both and see what you get.
As a free player you will get to reserve your in game character name and set up your account for the game right now.  You'll also get a news feed and a couple of in game items.  It's not bad if you really plan on playing the game when it comes out but honestly it's something that could have just as easily been done online.
Now if your willing to drop down $5.00 in support of the game this app will really open up quite a bit.  You'll get all the things a free player gets plus get your name in the game credits, get a few more in game items and titles, coolest of which is "Big Damn Hero," and you get a ship viewer to see ships that will be in game, a collectible virtual card collection with images from the TV show, and best of all, a map of the verse.  Along with the map of the verse comes a mini game where you do "trade runs," finding one planet then another and another.  There's practice, untimed ones, and a daily and weekly timed ones.  These mini-games give you more BP (brownie points) which will get you more cards for your collection and more in game items and titles.  The map of the verse can also be a great resource for those who do table top roleplaying in the Firefly universe as it gives you a zoomable view of the entire Firefly universe along with descriptions of each planet, some of them going into great detail.
There is also an option to support the game more by purchasing virtual card packs to help complete your collection.  These range from $0.99 to $2.99 depending on how many cards you want and the chance of rare or super rare card drops.  It's kind of a cool way to help support the game but not something that will make or break your app experience really if you decide to do it or not do it.
At the end of the day though it comes down to this...  Do you like Firefly and want to support a future game featuring it's universe??  If you don't then just go ahead and pass this app up.  But if you do enjoy Firefly and want more cool stuff about it you'll find a lot of enjoyment within the app, if your willing to give em your hard earned five bucks....
Edit:  Apparently the game has died.  Sucks as it could have been awesome.....

The main character's most obvious feature is an interesting way to tell a tale about how differences on the outside do not really matter compared to what is on the inside. In some ways, Sachi reminds me of Hanako from Katawa Shoujo or Aeka from Yume Miru Kusuri (though without the sheer hell that Aeka goes through... or the extremely satisfying way she snaps at her bully in the end [which was so deserved; seriously what that bully attempted...]).
I have to recommend this for any romantics out there. Or for that matter romance readers (it seriously is in the vein of some of the sweeter ones).

This isnt much different from any of the previous Football Manager games, and to be completely honest this review focuses more on the general issues of the game. The best summary of this game is that it merely gives you the illusion that your decisions and tactics are having an impact on the outcome of not only the game, but anything at all. A loophole within the game that involves saving the game before any match, and before the final whistle simply using Task Manager to close FM and then opening again at the point where you saved. This has allowed me to experiment with the mechanics of the game, altering my pre-match comments which only accurately represent the drama and controversy of Jose Mourinho's press conferences and no other manager. Also altering my tactics and even completely changing my team and also the morale (which can easily be boosted and lowered through simple interactions which rarely occur in real life). An example of a ridiculous interaction is that praising a player for playing well in a match can result in the player completely disagreeing with you and going from good morale to poor morale. No player is that sensitive - these are adults and FM treats them like they have the maturity of 7 year olds, anyway. So after altering a variety of things, i rentered the same match, and 9 out of 10 times i would receive the same result, often with similar patterns, e.g. comebacks, penatlies, red cards etc. This exposed to me how scripted this game is and how whatever i do i cannot beat the algorthms that dictate the game. One example is the 'get stuck in' instruction, this basically results in your oppostion receiving a penalty ever other game and your team receiving a red card eveyr 3 or 4 games. Yes this accuately represents real life football and that aggressive tackling can lead to these occurances, but the issue is the uniformity of the occurances and how 'fixed' the mechanics are. Another major issue is transfers, the value of players is so random, on occasions you have players like Juan Mata being sold for £105m and at other times players with values at around £15m are being sold for £3-4m due to transfer requests. The only thing FM does right with transfers is young high potential players which are valued almost perfectly, which brings me to ask, why can't they make a similiar system for the rest of players? Minor issues such as when players promises are broken such as not strengethening a certain position can have such massive effects on the whole club which just kills the realism of the whole game.
There are so many other issues within this game that i could rant about but i dont have all week, this review has felt almost like therapy.
FM17 however is still a decent game, compared to alternatives such as FIFA's Career Mode the detail is incomparable. But this doesen't excuse the game from its flaws and predictable game engine. Also we're paying £50 for this game but there isnt player faces or badges, seriously?! If your really thick and don't really notice that season after season your just following the same patterns then this game is perfect, but for you seasoned gamers this game is easily figured out after about 100 hours. But you would have probably got your money's worth by that point.
